### 5.2 E-functions and G-functions

Define `IsEFunction a` by algebraic coefficients a_n, D-finiteness of Σa_nzⁿ/n! over ℚ̄, geometric conjugate bounds |σa_n|≤C^(n+1), and common positive integral multipliers d_n≤D^(n+1) for a₀,…,a_n. Its analytic sum `eFun a` is entire. This uses geometric coefficient growth. (Fischler–Rivoal, Def. 1, p. 1; B08, §3.1, p. 11.)

Its API includes `ePowerSeries`: The power series Σ a_n zⁿ/n!; `eFun`: The entire function z ↦ Σ a_n zⁿ/n!; `hurwitzMul`: The binomial convolution, so that ePowerSeries (hurwitzMul a b)=ePowerSeries a · ePowerSeries b; `ePowerSeries_hurwitzMul`: ePowerSeries (hurwitzMul a b)=ePowerSeries a * ePowerSeries b; `IsEFunction.add`: Sums of E-functions are E-functions; `IsEFunction.hurwitzMul`: Products of E-functions are E-functions; `IsEFunction.shift`: The derivative (shifted coefficients) of an E-function is an E-function; `IsEFunction.map_ringEquiv`: Applying a ring automorphism σ of ℂ to the coefficients gives an E-function (the Galois conjugate f^σ); `IsEFunction.differentiable`: eFun a is entire; `IsEFunction.hasSum`: The series Σ a_n zⁿ/n! converges to eFun a z for every z; `IsEFunction.exists_numberField`: All coefficients lie in one number field.

**Checks.**

- The constant sequence 1 (the exponential) is an E-function.
- a_n=n − 1 ((z − 1)eᶻ) is an E-function.
- e^{z²} (a_{2k}=(2k)!/k!, a_{odd}=0) is not an E-function in this normalisation; Siegel's (n!)^ε definition would also reject it, but a definition bounding |a_n/n!| instead of |a_n| would accept it.
- a_n=n! (the series 1/(1 − z)) is not an E-function; forgetting the factorial normalisation would accept it.

*Needs:* §5.1.

Define `IsGFunction a` by the same algebraic, conjugate and denominator bounds, with D-finiteness of Σa_nzⁿ. Equivalently this ordinary series is G iff its factorial-divided series is E. It has positive convergence radius. (B08, §4.1, p. 18; Fischler–Rivoal, Def. 1, p. 2.)

Its API includes `isGFunction_iff_isEFunction`: IsGFunction a↔IsEFunction a (Borel transform); `IsGFunction.add`: Sums of G-functions; `IsGFunction.mul`: Cauchy products of G-functions; `IsGFunction.hasRadius`: A G-function converges on a disc of positive radius.

- Σ zⁿ (a_n=1) is a G-function.

- Σ zⁿ is a G-function exactly when Σ zⁿ/n!=eᶻ is an E-function.

*Needs:* §5.1.

No convergence claim is made for arbitrary coefficient sequences. (B08, §3.1, Prop. 3.2.1, pp. 11–12.)

- Constant data a_n=1 give the native formal exponential, with coefficient at n=2 equal to 1/2.

### 5.3 Differential systems and Galochkin denominators

Define `SolvesSystem T M F` on polynomial T, a finite square polynomial matrix M and a vector F of formal complex power series by TF_i′=Σ_jM_ijF_j. Its API proves closure under constant linear combinations of vector solutions for the same T,M, the component equations, multiplication of both T and M by a nonzero polynomial, and compatibility with the analytic differential equation wherever the series converge and T does not vanish. Every theorem interpreting this as F′=(M/T)F assumes T≠0. (B08, §2.2, p. 9; §4.4, p. 20.)

**Checks.**

- Formal exp solves the scalar system T=1,M=1.
- The same series fails T=1,M=0; constant series solve that system.
- T=M=0 makes the displayed relation hold for every F and supplies no differential equation, so T≠0 cannot be dropped from system interpretations.
- In dimension zero the vector equation is empty, with its unique empty solution.

Define `scaledDividedSystemIterates T M` by P₀=I and P_(m+1)=(T P′_m+P_mM−mT′P_m)/(m+1), with entrywise derivatives. For T≠0 and G=M/T these polynomial matrices equal T^m B_m, where y^(m)/m!=B_my. (B08, §4.4, p.20, §5.2, Lem. 5.2.1, p.22.)

### 5.5 Mahler systems and their values

Define `IsMahlerFunction` as follows. For integer q≥2 define `IsMahlerFunction q f` for a series with algebraic coefficients by Σi=0..n pᵢ(z)f(z^(qⁱ))=0 for nonzero polynomial data over ℚ̄. Equivalently f is a coordinate of F(z)=A(z)F(z^q), A∈GL_m(ℚ̄(z)). Use Mathlib’s `PowerSeries.expand r hr` for f(z^r), with hr:r≠0; its `expand_apply` identifies it with formal substitution by X^r. (AF17, §1, equation (1.1), p. 2; AF17, §1, p. 2.)

Its API includes `IsMahlerFunction.add`: Sums of q-Mahler functions are q-Mahler; `IsMahlerFunction.mul`: Products of q-Mahler functions are q-Mahler; `IsMahlerFunction.expand`: f(z^q) is q-Mahler if f is; `isMahlerFunction_of_polynomial`: Polynomials with algebraic coefficients are q-Mahler; `isMahlerFunction_iff_system`: f is q-Mahler iff it is the first coordinate of a solution of F(z)=A(z)F(z^q) with A invertible over ℂ(z) (and algebraic entries).

**Checks.**

- Σ z^{2^n} is 2-Mahler.
- A series with f=(1 − z)f(z²) and algebraic coefficients is 2-Mahler.
- For q≥2, exp is not q-Mahler: the functions exp(z^{q^i}) with distinct exponents have no nontrivial polynomial-coefficient linear relation. A predicate allowing arbitrary power-series coefficient relations would fail this test.
- z is q-Mahler (z^q·z − z·z^q=0 is trivial; use p₀=z^q, p₁=−z).
- A constant series with transcendental value c is not a Mahler function in this algebraic-coefficient convention, although it solves the one-dimensional identity system A=1. The system equivalence must retain the algebraic coefficients of F and A and q≥2.

Define `IsMahlerRegularPoint` as follows. Define `IsMahlerRegularPoint q A α` for a square matrix A over ℂ(z) by q≥2, det A≠0, 0<|α|<1 and absence of poles of entries of both A and A⁻¹ at every α^(q^ℓ), ℓ≥0. Poles use reduced rational denominators. Singularities have no accumulation in the open unit disc. (AF17, §1, p. 2.)

Its API includes `isMahlerRegularPoint_iff`: Unfolding: q≥2, det A≠0, 0 < |α| < 1 and no α^{q^ℓ} is a zero of the denominator of an entry of A or A⁻¹; `IsMahlerRegularPoint.pow`: α regular implies α^q regular; `isMahlerRegularPoint_of_polynomial`: For q≥2 and polynomial A with unit determinant every α in the punctured disc is regular.

**Checks.**

- For q≥2 and A=[[1, 0], [z, 1]] every 0 < |α| < 1 is regular.
- For A=(1 − 2z)⁻¹, α=2^{−1/2} is not regular; a definition testing only ℓ=0 would call it regular.
- For q≥2, the 0 × 0 system has determinant 1 and every point of the punctured disc is regular.
- The scalar zero matrix is not a regular system at 1/2, although all reduced entry denominators of A and its total inverse are 1. Testing denominators alone must not accept a singular matrix.
- For q=1 the identity matrix at 1/2 fails the q≥2 condition.

Every Mahler-system target below has q≥2 and an invertible matrix over ℚ̄(z).
All analytic targets start with a convergent germ: there is ρ>0 for
which each coefficient series is summable at every |z|<ρ. The formal predicate
alone does not stand for an analytic evaluation. Algebraic independence for
algebraic-coefficient germs over ℂ(z) is equivalent to absence of a nonzero
relation over ℚ̄[z], and their transcendence degrees over ℂ(z) and ℚ̄(z) agree.
(B08, Thm.3.3.1, p.13.)

from a convergent q-Mahler germ. Given a system F(z)=A(z)F(z^q), set

z^(q^ℓ) inside the initial convergence disc, and continue F by
A_ℓ(z)F(z^(q^ℓ)) as a meromorphic germ. Prove `mahler_iterate_independent`:
sufficiently deep iterates give the same germ, including across removable

**Algebraic closure of common constants.** Build `axConstantFieldClosure`.
Extend each Dⱼ uniquely from F to an algebraic closure F̄. For a separable
minimal polynomial p of a over F the extension satisfies
Dⱼa=−(Dⱼ applied to the coefficients of p)(a)/p′(a).
The common constants in F̄ are precisely C̄, the elements algebraic over C,
and C̄ is algebraically closed. Indeed, for a common constant a, differentiating
its monic minimal polynomial over F gives a polynomial of smaller degree
vanishing at a, so every coefficient belongs to C. Conversely, algebraic
elements over C are constants by separability. In particular F∩C̄=C.

logarithmic differentials and constant-coefficient relations. Construct it
through the separable algebraic tower comparisons; Mathlib's
KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale supplies the
formally étale comparison. The extension and comparison for arbitrary
algebraic towers, including their finite-subextension compatibility, belong
here. Rational independence of x modulo C is equivalent to independence
of its image modulo C̄, since rational sums of x remain in F.
Prove that trdeg_C C(x,y)=trdeg_C̄ C̄(x,y) and that every finite derivative
submatrix has unchanged rank after extending F to F̄. Thus the algebraically
closed-constant argument descends to the stated F and C.
(Kirby, §3.2, Proposition 3.5 and §3.3, Theorem 3.8, pp.33,37–38;
Stacks, Tag [090W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/090W), finite
separable extensions and formal étaleness; the minimal-polynomial
calculation above supplies the common-constant adapter.)

### Examples

The E-series for exp z has a_n=1, whereas the same analytic function has G-series coefficients 1/n!, which fail the denominator bound. The scaled system recurrence T=1,M=1 gives P₂=1/2. For the Laplace transform g=1/(x−1), xg−1=g; the initial-value correction is essential. The dependent tuple (1,2) in Schanuel has transcendence degree 1, so distinctness cannot replace ℚ-independence.

TauCetiRoadmap/FinancialMathematics:
# Financial mathematics: one-factor markets and replication

This roadmap owns one-factor asset markets, self-financing trading, replication and the Black–Scholes theorem. MarketImpact consumes this foundation and owns endogenous demand, equilibrium feedback, coupled pricing and its numerical models.

## Conventions

Time is calendar time t∈[0,T], T>0, and spot is s>0. Write C(s,t), with spot first, as in the Lean `Price` type. Remaining-maturity notation is f(s,τ)=C(s,T−τ). Asset drift is μ_S; income drift in MarketImpact is μ_Y; the MarketImpact source notation μ₁ is its model-specific instance. Holdings (a,b) mean numbers of stock and bond shares. The bond price is β, and bβ is the bond part of wealth. The market price of risk is κ; it is not a holding.

Work on a filtered probability space with the usual conditions and Brownian motion relative to that filtration. State filtration-relative increment independence; a native Brownian marginal-law predicate alone does not supply it. Equivalence of measures preserves completed null sets on the finite horizon.

## M0.1. Assets and trading

Let r_t be deterministic continuous, β₀>0 and β_t=β₀ exp(∫₀ᵗr_u du). For progressively measurable real μ_t,σ_t with ∫₀ᵀ(|μ_t|+σ_t²)dt<∞ almost surely, construct the unique strong solution of

`dS_t=μ_t S_t dt+σ_t S_t dW_t`,

for a positive F₀-measurable S₀, and prove

`S_t=S₀ exp(∫₀ᵗ(μ_u−σ_u²/2)du+∫₀ᵗσ_u dW_u)>0`.

No initial moment assumption is needed for existence/positivity. Moment estimates carry their own hypotheses. Consume [StochasticCalculus S9.4](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/1030)'s progressively measurable linear-SDE theorem, including its stochastic-integrand/localization and stopped integrating-factor uniqueness proofs. M0.1 supplies the positive asset initial value and the financial coefficient hypotheses, and identifies the resulting asset process. This includes σ_t=0, time-dependent deterministic coefficients and constant GBM. Trading, self-financing and admissibility remain financial contracts.

A strategy is a predictable pair (a_t,b_t) with stochastic integrability against S and pathwise integrability against β. Wealth is V_t=a_t S_t+b_t β_t. Define self-financing by

`V_t=V₀+∫₀ᵗa_u dS_u+∫₀ᵗb_u dβ_u`

simultaneously in t, after selecting continuous versions. Prove the simple-strategy formula for a_t=Σ_j a_{t_{j−1}}1_(t_{j−1},t_j], where a_{t_j} is F_{t_j}-measurable and supplies the following interval. Approximation and integral congruence give the general formula. Negative a means short stock; negative b means borrowing. Specify initial cost, terminal payoff and scaling of strategies. Trading costs and dividends are absent in this market.

## M0.2. Equivalent measure, completeness and no arbitrage

For constants r,μ_S and σ≠0, use β_t=e^{rt} and the augmented natural filtration of W. Put κ=(μ_S−r)/σ and

`Z_T=exp(−κW_T−κ²T/2)`, `dQ=Z_T dP`.

Prove that Z is a true positive martingale on [0,T], Q is an equivalent probability and W^Q_t=W_t+κt is Brownian under Q. Prove that the augmented natural filtrations of W and W^Q agree; deterministic path translation is invertible and P,Q have the same null sets. Consume S6.1's natural-Brownian L² martingale representation under Q on that filtration. An arbitrary larger filtration carrying Brownian motion is not declared complete.

The baseline admissible class consists of self-financing integrable strategies whose discounted wealth is a true square-integrable Q-martingale. Prove closure under finite linear combinations. For every F_T-measurable real claim H with e^{−rT}H∈L²(Q), construct its predictable replicating strategy, including the bond holding, and prove uniqueness of the value process

`V_t=e^{rt} E_Q[e^{−rT}H | F_t]`.

Define arbitrage as zero initial cost, nonnegative terminal wealth almost surely, and strictly positive terminal wealth with positive probability. Prove its absence in the baseline admissible class. Prove law of one price and the static-claim extension: if both signs of a claim can be traded at price p and the stock/bond replication costs q, p≠q gives a zero-cost arbitrage after placing the surplus in the bond. With unrestricted position scaling, the family of N-fold strategies yields unbounded sure profit; one fixed trade yields only its fixed surplus. State the scaling premise explicitly. This does not impose the baseline martingale condition on a mispriced added claim by definition.

Extend the completeness and pricing theorem to progressively measurable coefficients on the same augmented natural P-Brownian filtration. On each finite horizon assume deterministic constants `0<δ_σ≤C_σ<∞` and `K_κ≥0` with `δ_σ≤|σ_t|≤C_σ` and `|κ_t|≤K_κ` for Lebesgue-time×P almost every (t,ω), deterministic continuous r, and `κ_t=(μ_t−r_t)/σ_t` on this full-measure set. Consume StochasticCalculus S3.4 to choose predictable-equivalent versions of progressive σ and κ before forming the stochastic integrals, preserving the coefficient identities almost everywhere. Construct `Z=exp(−∫κdW−½∫κ²dt)`, prove it is a strictly positive true martingale, and define Q on the full horizon. Prove predictable representation under Q on the original filtration by the density/Bayes and Itô-product transformation of the P-representation, with localization for intermediate products. For random κ, do not infer that the natural filtrations of W and `W^Q=W+∫κdt` coincide. For F_T-measurable real H with `H/β_T∈L²(Q)` construct the Q-martingale `M_t=E_Q[H/β_T|F_t]`, its integrand h, wealth `V=βM`, and holdings `a=βh/(Sσ)`, `b=(V−aS)/β`. Verify predictable representatives and integrability under P as well as Q, self-financing and terminal convergence. Export the same no-arbitrage, uniqueness and static-claim results in this class. This theorem supplies variable-coefficient consumers; extensions from stopped/local coefficient bounds require separately proved full-horizon nonexplosion, true density and integrability conditions.

## M0.3. Classical price and the self-financing PDE

For deterministic continuous Markov coefficients μ_S(s,t),σ(s,t), r_t, assume a positive nonexplosive strong solution from every deterministic start (s₀,t₀). Let C be C^{2,1} on s>0, t<T, with derivatives continuous there and the stated terminal extension. Replication here means V_t=C(S_t,t) simultaneously throughout [t₀,T), almost surely, not merely equality at maturity.

On an open pricing domain where σ(s,t)≠0, identify a=C_s by the martingale part, set b=(C−sC_s)/β, and derive the necessary pointwise equation

`C_t+(σ(s,t)²s²/2)C_{ss}+r_t(sC_s−C)=0`.

First obtain the identity dt×P-almost everywhere along each solution. Continuity and the all-start hypothesis give the value at each starting point. A single initial trajectory supplies only the along-path statement. Conversely, only use a Q-based sufficiency criterion after M0.2 has constructed an equivalent measure Q on the declared filtration with the needed true-density and predictable-representation properties (including its variable-coefficient hypotheses when applicable). Under those hypotheses, use the following sufficient admissibility conditions: the candidate holdings have predictable representatives, are stochastically integrable against S and pathwise integrable against β on the full horizon, `C(S_t,t)/β_t` extends to a true square-integrable Q-martingale on [t₀,T], and `C(S_t,t)→h(S_T)` almost surely as t↑T. Prove replication with terminal value h(S_T), and identify its value with M0.2’s conditional price. Supply a usable derivative/moment criterion implying these conditions; for example `|C|+|sC_s|≤A(1+s^p)` uniformly, continuous terminal convergence and finite Q-moments of order 2p with corresponding full-horizon maximal bounds. The constant-coefficient call/put case follows with p=1 from GBM moments. Local Itô identities without these terminal and true-martingale conditions do not assert admissibility. Prescribed delta strategies give the drift identity even when σ vanishes; arbitrary replicating strategies in a degenerate market do not identify a=C_s. Do not assert the same necessity theorem there without a separate no-arbitrage/drift condition. The zero-volatility asset and deterministic bond cases remain part of M0.1.

General-coefficient PDE existence is a separate target in an explicit class: write y=log s, assume the pricing generator’s transformed risk-neutral drift r(t)−σ(e^y,t)²/2 and diffusion σ(e^y,t) are bounded parabolic C^α coefficients, α∈(0,1), globally Lipschitz in y uniformly in time, with 0<δ≤σ²≤Λ, and r∈C^{α/2}([0,T]). For terminal data h with h(e^y)/(1+e^y)∈C_b^{2+α}(ℝ), construct a classical solution with C(e^y,t)/(1+e^y) in C_b^{2+α,1+α/2}(ℝ×[0,T]), and prove uniqueness there. The transformation by the weight 1+e^y has bounded logarithmic derivatives. Own the localization/Feynman–Kac coefficient and growth adapters; consume [PDE Lane F27.3 and F27.6](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/959)’s classical whole-space parabolic Schauder theorem, including its bounded terminal operator and weight-conjugation estimate. The constant call/put theorem below has an independent direct proof and does not assume this general theorem for its nonsmooth payoff.

## M0.4. Black–Scholes calls, puts and analytic API

Fix r∈ℝ, σ>0, K>0, T>0. Define φ(z)=(2π)^(−1/2)e^(−z²/2) and Φ(z)=∫_(−∞)^z φ(u)du, using the native standard Gaussian measure and CDF. Prove its normalization, derivative, symmetry and tail identities through [StandardDistributions](../StandardDistributions/README.md)' Gaussian targets. For s>0, τ=T−t>0 put

`d_+=(log(s/K)+(r+σ²/2)τ)/(σ√τ)`, `d_−=d_+−σ√τ`,

`C(s,t)=sΦ(d_+)−Ke^(−rτ)Φ(d_−)`,

`P(s,t)=Ke^(−rτ)Φ(−d_−)−sΦ(−d_+)`.

Prove the PDE, put–call parity, risk-neutral payoff expectation and self-financing replication. Extend continuously to t=T by (s−K)_+ and (K−s)_+, respectively. The uniqueness class consists of classical solutions for s>0, 0≤t<T (right time derivative at t=0), continuous up to t=T and s=0, with |C(s,t)|≤A(1+s) uniformly. Prove uniqueness directly by stopped Itô on s∈[1/n,n] and GBM moment bounds, then pass to the limit by uniform integrability. This does not use a bounded-domain elliptic maximum principle as an unbounded parabolic uniqueness theorem.

Prove call boundary C(0,t)=0, put boundary P(0,t)=Ke^(−rτ), and far-field limits C(s,t)−s+Ke^(−rτ)→0 and P(s,t)→0. Prove call delta 0<C_s<1, call bond holding b=−Ke^(−rτ)Φ(d_−)/β_t<0, and the corresponding put delta and bond formulas. Prove positive call/put gamma and vega on s>0,t<T, with exact derivative formulas and terminal limits under their actual domains. For fixed s>0 distinct from K, gamma tends to zero as τ↓0. At s=K it diverges to +∞, with `√τ gamma(K,T−τ)→1/(Kσ√(2π))`; it has no finite pointwise terminal value there. The zero-feedback substitution in MarketImpact is algebraic; a parameter limit also requires its solution-dependence theorem.

## Dependencies and order

Use [StochasticCalculus](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/1030) S0.2 for versions and measurability, S3.2–S3.4 for the actual stochastic integrals, S5.1 for Itô, S5.4 for exponentials, S6.1 for natural-Brownian L² martingale representation, S7.3 for Bayes/density transformations, S7.4 for finite-horizon true-density Girsanov, and S9.4 for the progressive-coefficient linear-SDE solution, uniqueness and constant GBM specialization. M0.1 supplies its asset-model inputs and owns the trading/self-financing contracts. M0.2 follows those inputs. M0.3 uses M0.1 and Itô; its general existence consumes the [PDE Lane F27 proposal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/959)’s whole-space Schauder supplier. M0.4 uses the explicit Gaussian formulas, stopped Itô and GBM moments; S10.3's polynomial-growth theorem on ℝ^d is not silently applied to an exponentially growing function of log spot. [StandardDistributions](../StandardDistributions/README.md) owns the Gaussian CDF analytic identities. MarketImpact owns its nonlinear equilibrium, perturbation, noncompact minimum principle, fitting, and numerical theorem adapters.

The suggested Lean file pins price derivatives, drift algebra, deterministic exponential positivity, native Gaussian payoff integrability and the call payoff expectation identity. That identity is an admitted analytic theorem target. The README specifies the full market and replication contracts.

# Formal Laurent fields, Puiseux expansions and continuous differential calculus

Develop formal substitution, continuous derivations and residues, finite ramified
Laurent extensions, the characteristic-zero Newton–Puiseux algebraic closure,
and its procyclic absolute Galois group. Supply usable coefficient, topology,
coordinate-change and finite-extension APIs for formal connections and loop
algebras.

## Carriers, scope and suppliers

Use Mathlib's `PowerSeries K`, `LaurentSeries K = HahnSeries ℤ K`,
`LaurentPolynomial K = AddMonoidAlgebra K ℤ`, and `HahnSeries ℚ K`.
K is an arbitrary field in L1–L4 except where characteristic zero is explicitly
required. L5's Newton-polygon and coprime-factor-Hensel APIs hold over arbitrary
K; its root theorem and L6–L7 assume characteristic zero and K algebraically
closed. Put `ord = HahnSeries.orderTop`, including ord(0)=∞;
ord(t)=1. Mathlib's multiplicative `LaurentSeries.valued` has v(t)=exp(−1).

The Puiseux field is the subfield of `HahnSeries ℚ K` whose support has a single
positive common denominator: for some n>0, every supported exponent is k/n,
k∈ℤ. It is the union of embedded K((t^(1/n))) under divisibility transition
maps. Construct it on this carrier. Define `RamificationIndex` as a type
synonym of ℕ+ with order n≤m meaning n|m, independently of ℕ+'s usual order.
In L4 form the level diagram in `CommAlgCat K` on its thin category.
Prove there that its cocone into Puiseux is a colimit: every compatible family of
K-algebra maps into any commutative K-algebra factors uniquely through it.

[Dean Cureton's formal Puiseux development](https://github.com/deancureton/Puiseux)
constructs this directed-union carrier and proves algebraicity and algebraic
closedness (`PuiseuxSeries.isAlgClosure`). It is an existing implementation
candidate for L4–L5, independent of Tau Ceti's analytic Puiseux results. Coordinate
with its author before integrating code, following this repository's porting
policy. The targets below specify the mathematics whether developed independently
or integrated; retain their full coefficient, topology, differential and Galois
APIs rather than stopping at the closure theorem.

## L1. Formal substitutions and coordinate groups

Expose the constant-field, polynomial, power-series and Laurent-field maps as
a compatible algebra tower. Construct the Laurent-polynomial embedding by
its finite sum of monomials. Prove injectivity, coefficient formulas, image
and order characterizations. Identify K[[t]] with the nonnegative-order
valuation ring, its maximal ideal with positive order and residue with constant
coefficient. Prove Laurent-polynomial density and truncation convergence:
f_i→f iff for every a, eventually ord(f_i−f)≥a. Equivalently, the supports
are eventually uniformly bounded below and each coefficient eventually equals
the corresponding coefficient of f. Prove this by stabilization of the finite
interval between the support bound and a. The sequence t^(−j), j≥1, has
coefficientwise eventual zero but fails valuation convergence.

For every nonzero φ∈tK[[t]] construct substitution on K[[t]] and extend to F
using f=t^(−N)f₊. Prove independence of N, K-algebra-map laws, composition,
injectivity and ord(f(φ))=ord(φ)ord(f) for f≠0. Supply continuity, coefficient
formulas and the ramified substitution t↦s^e, e>0, between two copies of F.

Coordinates are those φ with nonzero linear coefficient. Give K[[t]] the
subspace valuation topology from F through a scoped instance in a named namespace,
with its inclusion into F an `IsInducing` map. Keep this scope distinct from
`PowerSeries.WithPiTopology`; introduce no global topology instance. Construct their
K-algebra automorphism group of K[[t]] with multiplication σ·τ=σ∘τ.
Writing σ_φ(f)=f(φ), pin σ_φ∘σ_ψ=σ_(ψ(φ)); thus the parameter-series
composition group maps anti-isomorphically to this automorphism group.
Construct inverses and prove this parameter dictionary. Prove such automorphisms preserve the maximal ideal
and are automatically continuous. Obtain inverse coefficients recursively:
the degree-n composition equation determines b_n by the nonzero linear term,
and prove uniqueness. For each N≥1 define the N-jet group as these substitutions
modulo t^(N+1), give composition and truncation maps, and prove the full group
is their inverse limit, with the jet groups discrete and the coordinate group
given the topology of agreement modulo each t^(N+1). Define infinitesimal substitutions as K[ε]-algebra automorphisms of
`PowerSeries (DualNumber K)`, reducing to identity and preserving (t); identify their ε-coefficients with
tK[[t]]D. Prove every K-derivation K[[t]]→K[[t]] is t-adically continuous:
δ(t^n f)=nt^(n−1)fδ(t)+t^nδ(f) gives δ((t^n))⊆(t^(n−1)).
Truncation then determines δ from δ(t), including in positive characteristic. Over `DualNumber (DualNumber K)`, identified with
K[ε₁,ε₂]/(ε₁²,ε₂²), with σ₁=1+ε₁aD and σ₂=1+ε₂bD,
prove σ₁σ₂σ₁⁻¹σ₂⁻¹=1+ε₁ε₂(aDb−bDa)D. This pins the operator-commutator
sign. For every coefficient-field embedding K→K′, use coefficientwise
power/Laurent maps and prove naturality of substitution and jet truncation.

## L2. Continuous derivations and one-forms

Prove product, inverse and quotient rules for the existing Laurent derivative
D, compatibility with power-series derivatives and Hasse derivatives, and the
chain rule for all L1 substitutions. Prove ord(Df)≥ord(f)−1 and continuity.
For f≠0 with leading exponent r and coefficient a_r≠0, if r has nonzero
image in K prove coeff_(r−1)(Df)=r a_r and ord(Df)=r−1. When that image vanishes, locate the first
exponent with nonzero differentiated coefficient, or prove Df=0. In
characteristic zero prove ker D=K.

Use Mathlib's `Derivation K F F`; take the submodule of maps continuous for the
valuation topology. Prove each is uniquely aD, a∈F, and conversely every aD is
continuous. Prove bracket closure and [aD,bD]=(aDb−bDa)D. Characterize the
K[[t]]-preserving and maximal-ideal-preserving subalgebras as respectively
K[[t]]D and tK[[t]]D, with the L1 infinitesimal-coordinate comparison.

Package D as a `Derivation K F F` using its product rule.
Let λ:Ω[F/K]→F be `D.liftKaehlerDifferential`. Define Ω¹_cont(F/K) as
Ω[F/K]/ker λ and prove the induced F-linear equivalence with F, sending dt
to 1. Give it the transported valuation module topology. For a finite-dimensional
Hausdorff F-module M with `IsModuleTopology F M`, prove continuous K-derivations F→M
factor uniquely through this quotient by a continuous F-linear map. Establish
continuity of factorization and of the quotient derivation. The construction factors the algebraic Kähler derivation through the
specified quotient, identifying its dt class with 1.
Prove coordinate covariance du=Dφ dt, functoriality and compatibility with
coefficientwise field embeddings K→K′;
for coordinate automorphisms this gives an invertible semilinear map on forms.

## L3. Residue, primitives and coefficient duality

Define Res(f dt)=coeff_(−1) f. Prove linearity, vanishing on U_0 dt,
Res(dg)=0 and Res(f dg)=−Res(g df). Prove for every nonzero φ∈tK[[t]] of
order e the finite-map formula Res(f(φ)Dφ dt)=e Res(f dt), in all
characteristics. In particular coordinate changes preserve residue. Build the
universal coefficient identity, for a commutative ring R, a unit u∈R[[t]]ˣ
and e,k≥1:

`e·coeff_(ek)(u^(−k)) + coeff_(ek−1)(u^(−k−1)u′) = 0`.

Prove inverse/product/derivative compatibility with `PowerSeries.map` and
finite-jet dependence of these coefficients. In the universal ring
ℤ[x₀,…,x_(ek)][x₀⁻¹], prove the identity by passage to its characteristic-zero
fraction field and injectivity, then specialize x_j to the coefficients of u
in R. For φ=t^e u this treats all negative monomials except t^(−1), whose
residue is e; nonnegative monomials have zero residue. Extend by valuation
continuity. AlgebraicCurves Layer 9 transports this coordinate-level formula
along its completion charts.

In characteristic zero construct a primitive of every residue-zero form by
termwise division, prove uniqueness modulo K, and characterize im D as exactly
these forms. Include negative exponents and the excluded t^(−1) coefficient.
The t^(−1) form remains outside the derivative image.

Prove nondegeneracy of (f,g)↦Res(fg dt), annihilator(U_a)=U_(−a), and perfect
finite-dimensional pairings U_a/U_b × U_(−b)/U_(−a), a≤b. For finite-dimensional
K-vector spaces V use `HahnModule ℤ K V` for V((t)) with its F-module action,
and the coefficient-preserving `HahnModule.of` comparison to `LaurentSeries V`.
Topologize it by the K-linear lattices U_a=t^aV[[t]], consisting of series
with every coefficient below a zero; these are K[[t]]-submodules. Prove the natural F-linear comparison F⊗_K V≃V((t)) for finite-dimensional V,
using the singleton constant-coefficient map; prove finite-basis independence,
completeness and the power-series lattice/finite-jet comparisons. Identify its
continuous K-linear dual with V*((t))dt by coefficient contraction and residue.
Define the dual topology by annihilators of U_(−a)(V); prove this identification
is a homeomorphism and compatible with linear maps. The dt factor gives the
coordinate-covariant description; changing parameters transforms forms too.

Compare Laurent-polynomial derivative/residue with the Laurent embedding.
For every K-Lie algebra L, construct the K-linear map
`AddMonoidAlgebra K ℤ ⊗[K] L → HahnModule ℤ K L` sending t^j⊗v to the
coefficient-j singleton v. Define the bracket directly by coefficient
convolution on `HahnModule ℤ K L` for every K-Lie algebra L; prove the
coefficient sums finite and the support bounded below, and establish the Lie
identities over K. For finite-dimensional L give F⊗_K L its scalar-extended
F-Lie algebra and L((t)) its coefficientwise F-action, then prove the
comparison is an F-`LieEquiv`. Transport `LaurentSeries.derivative K` on `LaurentSeries L`
through `HahnModule.of` to define D on L((t)); prove continuity and
D(f·v)=Df·v+f·Dv. Prove coefficient formulas, injectivity, bracket compatibility and
functoriality. Extend a K-bilinear form Φ coefficientwise
and prove that Res(Φ(f,Dg)dt), restricted along this polynomial-loop embedding,
is Mathlib's `LieAlgebra.LoopAlgebra.residuePairing Φ`, including
its coefficient n on a second argument of degree n. These are the exact
supplier identities for formal loop cocycles.

## L4. Ramified levels and the Puiseux field

For n>0 construct ι_n:K((u))→K⟦ℚ⟧ using `HahnSeries.embDomainAlgHom` on
k↦k/n, with coefficient, support and injectivity theorems. For n|m construct
u_n↦u_m^(m/n), prove composition and compatibility with ι_n and ι_m.
Identify level-n images by denominator n, intersections by gcd, and generated
composita by lcm. Prove every finite family of Puiseux elements lies in a
single common level, with a common-level lift for polynomial coefficients.
Prove closure of their union under addition, multiplication and inverse, and install the resulting subfield's K- and level-one F-algebra
structures with the tower laws.

Over F, prove level n has basis 1,u,…,u^(n−1): split an arbitrary Laurent
series into its n exponent congruence classes and prove uniqueness. Thus its
degree is n and every Puiseux element is algebraic over F in all
characteristics. Identify the level with adjoining a root of X^n−t, and prove
irreducibility by this basis or the valuation-ring Eisenstein/Gauss argument.
Supply the substitution comparison to L1's t↦u^n.

Restrict `HahnSeries.addVal` to obtain the Puiseux additive valuation in
`WithTop ℚ`, and compare with each level's integer order scaled by 1/n.
Supply its multiplicative valuation in `WithZero (Multiplicative ℚ)`, sending
a nonzero series of order q to `WithZero.exp (−q)` and zero to zero;
use its valuation topology and prove level
embeddings are homeomorphisms onto their images. Prove the Puiseux field is
not complete: the partial sums of Σ_(j≥1) t^(j+1/(j+1)) are Puiseux elements
and form a valuation-Cauchy sequence, while its Hahn-series limit has no finite
common denominator. Prove coefficient uniqueness excludes any Puiseux limit.
This also exhibits its strict inclusion in the full rational Hahn field.

In characteristic zero define D_t on this subfield by the coefficient rule
D_t(t^q)=q t^(q−1). Prove its support remains at a finite level, level
compatibility, continuity and product/chain identities. Under ι_n,
D_t(ι_n f)=(1/n)u^(1−n)ι_n(D_u f). Define one-forms by the same continuous
quotient construction at each level, with compatible transition maps.
With dt=n u^(n−1)du prove Res_u(f dt)=n Res_t(f dt), where Res_t on Puiseux
means rational-exponent coefficient −1. Prove its residue-zero primitive
criterion and coordinate/substitution comparisons.

## L5. Newton polygons and formal Newton–Puiseux

For polynomials over F construct coefficient Newton polygons, faces/slopes and
initial polynomials. Supply translation, scaling, the Minkowski-sum formula for
Newton polygons of nonzero products (equivalently union of slope multisets), coefficient
valuation bounds and ramified-substitution APIs. Consume the existing
`IsAdicComplete.henselianRing`/simple-root Hensel theorem for K[[t]], proving
the reduction hypotheses needed. Consume the existing instance
`IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {PowerSeries.X}) (PowerSeries K)` and compare that
ideal to the maximal ideal. Build the monic
coprime-factor lifting theorem as an explicit target: from a factorization
of the reduction into coprime monic factors, lift uniquely to monic factors
of the same degrees. Give the recursive coefficient correction by Bézout and
polynomial division, prove coefficientwise compatibility and completeness,
and compare its degree-one specialization to the existing simple-root theorem.

For algebraically closed K of characteristic zero prove every nonconstant
polynomial over F has a root at a finite L4 level. Normalize to monic and clear
poles by scaling the unknown. At a monic polynomial of degree m, remove its
degree-(m−1) coefficient by a Tschirnhaus shift. Write the translated
polynomial as P=Y^m+Σ_(i=2)^m a_i Y^(m−i). If every a_i=0, the root is
zero; otherwise choose the minimum ord(a_i)/i over its nonzero coefficients a_i,
ramify t=s^q to clear that slope's denominator, rescale Y=s^p Z and divide
by s^(pm). Prove the transformed polynomial is monic over K[[s]], still has
zero degree-(m−1) coefficient, and its reduction has a nonzero lower term.
Its reduction therefore cannot be (Z−a)^m: for a≠0 the coefficient −ma
is nonzero in characteristic zero, and for a=0 it has no lower term. Choose
a nonzero root and split off its multiplicity-r factor, with 0<r<m and
coprime complement. Apply the specified factor-Hensel target to obtain a
monic degree-r factor and recurse. Termination is strict degree descent.
Track all substitution/inverse transformations and finite ramification levels;
the final degree-one factor gives a root in one complete level. Include
polynomials with repeated roots and negative slopes after Laurent normalization. The
coprime-factor lifting theorem and polynomial transformations are built before
this degree induction.

For a polynomial over Puiseux, first lift its finite coefficient family to one
common level from L4, reinterpret that level as K((u)), apply the root theorem
there, and compare the resulting level-nm embedding to the original Hahn
carrier. Deduce splitting, algebraic closedness and identification of the
Puiseux field as an algebraic closure of F using L4's finite-degree algebraicity.
Include polynomials with repeated roots and nonmonic polynomials. Examples must compute X^n−t,
fractional leading orders and distinct branches with a common initial term.
The sharp minimal-level bound and the resulting degree-factorial bound are L6
targets following the finite-extension classification.

## L6. Finite extensions, trace and compatible roots

Assume K algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Use L4's degree-n root
adjunction and Mathlib's `autEquivRootsOfUnity`, `autEquivZmod` and
`isGalois_of_isSplittingField_X_pow_sub_C` after identifying level n as the
splitting field of X^n−t. Prove the Kummer action u↦ζu, restriction formulas
and fixed fields on the actual Hahn-level carrier, consuming generic Kummer
and Galois correspondence rather than rebuilding them.

Every finite extension embeds in a level by L5 and finite generation. Prove
it is isomorphic over F to K((t^(1/e))) by cyclic Galois correspondence. These
are chosen AlgEquiv maps between field constructions. Compute the residue
field K, ramification index e, integer ring and valuation comparisons directly
from their exponent decomposition; no finite-residue hypothesis is used.
For a root α of a degree-d polynomial its minimal level equals [F(α):F]≤d,
so α lies at a level dividing d!, and all roots can be placed at level d!.

Construct trace on differentials via Ω¹_cont(L/K)=L⊗_F Ω¹_cont(F/K), prove
this equivalence for the finite separable level map, and prove
Res_F(Tr_(L/F) ω)=Res_L(ω). Verify the formula on u-monomials and extend by
continuity. Prove that the finite-extension residue is independent of the chosen
F-algebra equivalence with K((u)): compare its parameter-root images, then use
L3 coordinate invariance. State the corollaries
Res_F(Tr_(L_e/F)ω)=e Res_t^ℚ(ω) and Res_(u_m)=(m/n)Res_(u_n) under n|m,
while Res_t^ℚ is compatible with the Hahn transition inclusions. Distinguish the coefficient-−1 Res_t on rational exponents from
Res_u: the latter includes the factor e when a form is expressed with dt.

Construct primitive roots ζ_n∈K for every n>0, compatible by
ζ_m^(m/n)=ζ_n when n|m, and prove existence. For K=ℂ use exp(2πi/n).
Use a fresh type synonym for each finite group μ_n(K) and give it the
discrete topology, independently of any topology on K or its units. Construct
the inverse limit in `ProfiniteGrp` of these finite discrete groups, with
transition ζ↦ζ^(m/n), as their compatible-family closed subgroup of the
product. Prove its profinite structure, and construct the induced compatible
coefficientwise action on every Puiseux level, faithfulness and fixed fields.

## L7. Absolute Galois topology and parameter independence

Use Mathlib's Krull-topology carriers and
`InfiniteGalois.continuousMulEquivToLimit` on the L5 algebraic closure.
Prove the ramified levels are cofinal among finite Galois intermediate fields,
and give the cofinal-limit comparison to L6's μ_n limit. Consume Mathlib's
compactness/Hausdorff and inverse-limit theorems. Identify finite-level
stabilizers and transport to Mathlib's chosen `AlgebraicClosure F` through a
chosen F-algebra equivalence. Prove that the induced Galois-group comparison
and normalized generator are independent of this choice: two choices differ
by a Galois automorphism, and conjugation is trivial by L6's abelian group.

The compatible roots define the automorphism σ_ζ by u_n↦ζ_n u_n. Use
`TauCeti.zHat.lift σ_ζ` into the profinite Galois group. Consume
`zHat.lift_surjective` and `lift_injective_of_finite_quotients`, proving their
generator/detection hypotheses using the finite-level coordinates and obtain inverse continuity by compact-to-T2.
Thus Gal(F)≃ₜ*TauCeti.zHat with the generator sent to σ_ζ. Changing the
primitive-root system changes this coordinate by a unit of the profinite
integer ring; consume `TauCeti.zHat.existsUnique_forall_toZMod_eq`,
`TauCeti.zpowHat_eq_pow_val_toZMod` and `TauCeti.zHat.unitsLift` for the
compatible finite-level coordinates, exponent action and unit comparison.
Prove the action and inverse formulas.

Prove every unit in K[[t]] has an n-th root there, for n>0, using its constant
root and simple-root Hensel. Consequently the character
θ_n(g)=g(π^(1/n))/π^(1/n) is independent of the chosen uniformizer π and
of its chosen n-th root. Prove compatibility in n. A K-linear formal parameter
automorphism lifts to the algebraic closure; any two lifts induce the same
conjugation on the abelian Galois group, and this conjugation is identity by
the θ_n comparisons. The whole absolute Galois group is inertia here. Only
the identification with the specified generator of zHat uses ζ.

## Order and boundaries

L1→L2→L3 is independent of Newton–Puiseux. L4's embeddings and basis depend
on L1; its differential refinement uses L2–L3 and characteristic zero.
L5→L6→L7 follows that finite-level foundation. Every new object has
extensionality, composition, transport and its coefficient/topology formulas
before use downstream.

Positive-characteristic algebraic-closure descriptions, mixed-characteristic
local fields, analytic branch convergence, Stokes data, formal connections,
opers, affine central extensions and categorical Langlands statements are
outside this roadmap's scope. Tau Ceti's analytic Puiseux results concern analytic branch convergence and
have their own analytic hypotheses.

# Free probability, free products, and random matrix models

Build noncommutative distributions and free independence as usable theories,
with reduced and amalgamated operator-algebraic products, full Fock-space
models, noncrossing cumulants, additive and multiplicative convolution,
free limit theorems, and Gaussian and Haar random-matrix asymptotic freeness.
The combinatorial and analytic constructions must agree: a law computed by
cumulants must be realized by positive states where positivity is asserted,
and a matrix limit must specify which moments and convergence mode it proves.

## Scope, conventions, and dependencies

The algebraic theory uses unital complex algebras and complex-linear
functionals φ with φ(1)=1. A *-probability space additionally has an
involution and `φ(a*a)≥0`; a C*-probability space uses a unital C*-algebra
and an existing positive continuous linear functional with φ(1)=1. A
tracial state satisfies `φ(ab)=φ(ba)`. Faithfulness means
`φ(a*a)=0 → a=0`, and is a separate hypothesis. A W*-probability space
uses a von Neumann algebra and a specified normal state; require its
faithfulness or traciality in the results that use them. Algebraic
expectations are not silently positive or traces.

Use Mathlib's `Algebra`, `LinearMap`, `Subalgebra`, `StarSubalgebra`,
`PositiveLinearMap`, `FreeAlgebra`, `IncidenceAlgebra`, `Finpartition`,
`Polynomial`, `PowerSeries`, probability measures and Bochner integrals.
C*-states use `A →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ` with φ(1)=1, matching V0 and
`PositiveLinearMap.GNS`; consume their automatic continuity and norm-one
interfaces when a continuous-functional view is needed. A joint algebraic distribution
of `(a_i)` is `φ ∘ FreeAlgebra.lift ℂ a`; its *-distribution evaluates
words in generators and their adjoints. Use a type synonym of `FreeAlgebra ℂ (ι×Bool)` for the *-polynomials
and install its conjugate-linear involution by conjugating coefficients, reversing words,
and exchanging a generator with its formal adjoint. Do not reuse the
default `StarRing (FreeAlgebra R X)` from `Algebra.Star.Free`, which fixes
coefficients and generators; the synonym carries its own `StarRing` and
`StarModule ℂ` instances. Prove its universal
property and compatibility with evaluation. Commutative multivariate
polynomials do not encode arbitrary noncommutative words.

Inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument. Products in a
word follow its displayed order; in Lean use ordered lists, not an unordered
product in a noncommutative algebra. Write `tr_N=N⁻¹ Tr` for normalized
matrix trace. Our semicircular element is `s(h)=ℓ(h)+ℓ(h)*`, of variance
`‖h‖²` and support `[−2‖h‖,2‖h‖]`; this is twice the element normalized
by one-half in Voiculescu–Dykema–Nica. Creation operators satisfy
`ℓ(h)*ℓ(k)=⟪h,k⟫ I` in the second-variable-linear convention.

Cumulants κ_n have n≥1. The scalar law R-transform is
`R(z)=Σ_(n≥1) κ_n z^(n−1)`. The multivariable R-series has no constant
term and has κ_n as its degree-n coefficients; its one-variable version
is zR(z). State which of these conventions an identity uses. Analytic
measure transforms here concern compactly supported probability measures.
Formal identities have their own coefficient-wise proofs and do not assert
global invertibility of analytic transforms.

F1–F2 are the algebraic/combinatorial foundation. F3–F4 realize free
families, F5 builds convolution and transforms, F6–F7 develop their laws,
and F8 supplies matrix approximations.
Factor/subfactor applications motivate the tracial amalgamated products
and free Gaussian interfaces. Factor rigidity, index, planar-algebra and
classification theorems are outside these milestones. Free entropy, the
isomorphism problem for free-group factors, general unbounded-law analytic
subordination, non-Gaussian Wigner ensembles, almost-sure random-matrix
convergence, and strong convergence of random-matrix operator norms are
outside this roadmap. [Suggested.lean](Suggested.lean) gives representative
interfaces; this README is the specification.

whose finite combinatorial prerequisite and Milestones 1,3,5,6 already
specify the common scalar/matrix foundations. The overlapping targets
below refine those same reusable interfaces, with the generality and
conventions specified here; implement each common construction once.
They are milestone dependencies, not a dependency on its later local-law,
large-deviation or stochastic developments. Build any missing supplier
targets in Tau Ceti without waiting for that PR.

For F8's expected empirical measures consume RandomMatrices Milestone 1's
`empiricalMeasure`/`spectralMeasure` and decreasing Hermitian eigenvalues.
Prove its trace-moment dictionary and measurability comparison with the
all-moments quotient. Moment-to-weak convergence uses Milestone 3's common
